original_question: For which billiards, and under which joint limits of long time t and small hole size h, does the survival probability P(t) reduce to a function only of the combined variable h t?
target_in_paper: Open problem 4 / Problem 11.4 ("Scaling") in Section 4 / 11.4: "For what billiards and in what limits does P(t) reduce to a function of ht for a family of billiards with variable hole size h?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's main variables and almost exactly matches the official problem: it asks about open billiards, the joint long-time/small-hole regime, the survival probability P(t), and the one-parameter scaling variable ht. It is very close to the paper's own wording.
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem called "Scaling," not as a theorem or conjecture.
The scope is specifically open billiards, not general open dynamical systems.
The paper phrases the question for a family of billiards with variable hole size h.
The survival probability is defined earlier as P(t)=mu_0(Omega_t), where Omega_t={x in Omega : Phi^s(x) notin H for all s in (0,t]}.
The hole-size parameter is defined for billiards as h=|H|/|M| (for general maps, |H|/|Omega|).
The initial measure mu_0 is implicitly the natural equilibrium measure for the billiard flow or billiard map in the surrounding discussion.
For billiards, continuous time is the default unless otherwise stated.

The immediate motivation is the simultaneous-limit regime in the circle example with h->0 and t->infinity while ht is held constant; the paper then asks more generally which billiards and which limits exhibit this scaling.
Nearby context also notes that fixed ht is not universally the correct scaling limit, because the stadium example later in the section violates that naive scaling.
refined_question: Let H be a hole in an open billiard, let h=|H|/|M| denote its relative size, let Omega_t={x in Omega : Phi^s(x) notin H for all s in (0,t]}, and let P(t)=mu_0(Omega_t) be the survival probability for the natural equilibrium initial measure mu_0. For a family of open billiards with variable hole size h, for which billiards, and in which asymptotic regimes of simultaneously small hole and long time, does P(t) asymptotically reduce to a one-parameter scaling form F(ht), i.e. depend only on the product ht?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's official Open problem 4 / Problem 11.4 in the integrable-billiards part of Section 4 / 11.4. The wording there is essentially the same as your draft. To make it stand-alone, one must import the earlier definitions of Omega_t, P(t), mu_0, and h from Section 3 / 11.3. The immediate lead-in is the circle example, where taking h and t simultaneously so that ht stays constant appears numerically to produce a limiting function; the later stadium example shows that holding ht fixed is not always the right scaling, so the paper asks for a characterization of exactly which billiards and which limits have this property.
